discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 3008cec: directory listings carry a per-path generation, so a response that a newer listing has superseded is dropped. Interval polls skip folders still loading rather than superseding them, which keeps slow SSH listings from being cancelled forever. Test holds an old root listing, lands a newer one, then resolves the old one and checks the fresh entries stay.

Fixed in c739776f. The overview fetch now carries a generation (same pattern as the usage fetch): `loadOverview` captures it and checks it after every await, before any state write, and Sign Out bumps it. A response that lands after Sign Out therefore never reaches `applyAccountUser`, so the signed-out account cannot be written back into the context or its localStorage cache.

Sign Out also clears `overviewLoading` itself, since the stale fetch no longer clears it on the way out (the signed-out prompt would otherwise stay behind the spinner).

Test: `AccountView sign-out > drops an overview fetch that lands after sign-out` loads a user, starts a second overview load via an org switch, signs out, then resolves the pending `fetchMe` with the old user and asserts `applyAccountUser` ran once and the signed-out prompt is showing. Reverting the guard makes it fail with `applyAccountUser` called twice.

+/**
+ * Home-screen chooser for where the next task runs. Lives above the composer
+ * (not in it) so the live-chat controls stay uncluttered: Local | Cloud, and
+ * for Cloud the GitHub repository and branch (prefilled from the open
+ * workspace's origin remote) or the onboarding steps when GitHub isn't set up.
+ */
+export function TaskTargetPanel() {
+	const { cloudTaskTarget, workspaceRoots, primaryRootIndex } = useExtensionState()
+	const { clineUser } = useClineAuth()
+	const { handleSignIn } = useClineSignIn()
+	const signedIn = !!clineUser?.uid
+	const target = cloudTaskTarget?.target ?? "local"
+	const isCloud = target === "cloud"
+
+	const { connection, loading, refresh } = useGitHubConnection(isCloud && signedIn)
+	const [waitingForGitHub, setWaitingForGitHub] = useState(false)
+	const [workspaceDefaults, setWorkspaceDefaults] = useState<{ repoUrl?: string; branch?: string }>()
+	const [branches, setBranches] = useState<string[]>([])
+	const [branchesLoading, setBranchesLoading] = useState(false)
+	const branchRequest = useRef(0)
+

+	const selectedRepo = useMemo(

+			),

+	)
+
+	const persist = useCallback((selection: CloudTaskTargetSelection) => {
+		CloudServiceClient.setCloudTaskTarget(
+			CloudTaskTarget.create({
+				target: selection.target,
+				repoUrl: selection.repoUrl,
+				repositoryId: selection.repositoryId,
+				branch: selection.branch,
+			}),
+		).catch((error) => console.error("Failed to save task target:", error))
+	}, [])
+

+	useEffect(() => {
+		if (!isCloud) {
+			return
+		}

+			.then((defaults) => setWorkspaceDefaults({ repoUrl: defaults.repoUrl, branch: defaults.branch }))
+			.catch(() => setWorkspaceDefaults({}))
+	}, [isCloud, workspaceRoots, primaryRootIndex])
+
+	// The stored repository belongs to whichever account chose it. Once the
+	// current account's repositories are known and the stored one is not among
+	// them, drop it, so the composer does not treat a repository this account
+	// never selected as ready to submit.
+	useEffect(() => {

+			return

+		}

+		} finally {

+				setBranchesLoading(false)
+			}
+		}

discussion_comments.comment_body: Right; the unfiltered list is paginated and the first page cannot decide. Folded into 782e9d10d: the panel now asks GitHub for the workspace branch by name (listBranches already supports query) and suggests it only if that query returns it while the default branch is still selected. persist also takes an updater so the write after the async check reads the current selection rather than one captured before it.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 4730ce9bb by removing the class of bug rather than this instance. The webview no longer computes or writes the target at all. The extension stores only the user's choices (Local/Cloud, a repository, a branch), one field per click, and resolves the repository and branch on every state post from the account's repositories and the workspace remote. The branch check is a cached read, never a write, so a lookup that lands after Local was chosen cannot flip the target back. `sdk-cloud-task-target.test.ts` "keeps Local when a lookup lands after the user chose it" covers this.

Agreed, good catch. Fixed in f92a94ca3. The unmount-only cleanup in `useChatSession` now also sets `streamFlushTimerRef.current = null` after clearing the timer, so once the app is shown again `schedulePendingStreamFlush()` arms a new timer, and any text buffered before the hide goes out with the next flush. I made the same change to the `turnEndReconcileTimerRef` cleanup for consistency; that one couldn't stall, since its scheduler always clears and re-arms. New test: `keeps flushing streamed text after the app is hidden and restored` hides and restores the hook with `<Activity>` while a flush is pending. Without the fix the assistant message stays empty; with it, the text arrives.

Valid, fixed in 238f80630. This is the same pattern as the stream-flush timer: the unmount-only cleanup in `SpeechInput` cancels the recording, but Activity keeps `isListening`/`isProcessing`. The cleanup now also resets both flags, so `onActiveChange(false)` reaches the composer when the app is shown again. Setting state there is a no-op on a real unmount. New test `returns to inactive after an Activity hides it mid-recording` starts a streaming session, hides and shows the app, and checks the session was cancelled and the button is back to "Record speech" and enabled. It fails without the fix.

Fixed in 0093e45f1. The mouse and Ctrl+V paths now share a single `pasteFromClipboard` callback with one in-flight guard (same shape as `InputBar`): it returns early while a read is pending and releases the ref 100ms after settling, so two rapid right/middle clicks or a repeated Ctrl+V can no longer append the same clipboard contents twice.

The bracketed-paste path (`usePaste`) is left unguarded deliberately — it receives the text inline from the paste event and performs no async clipboard read, so there is no duplicate-read window there.
